    <div class="pub-item">
      <div class="pub-title"><a href="intro_to_r.html">Introduction to R</a></div>
      <div class="pub-venue">What R is, how to install it, and the core building blocks — arithmetic, objects, vectors, matrices, and data frames. Start here if you are new to R.</div>
    </div>

  </div>

  <div class="pub-year-group">
    <div class="pub-year-header">Script 2</div>

    <div class="pub-item">
      <div class="pub-title"><a href="../psy371/r_basics_psych.html">Descriptives, Correlation &amp; Regression</a></div>
      <div class="pub-venue">A complete data analysis workflow: importing a real psychology dataset, computing descriptive statistics with <code>psych::describe()</code>, testing correlations with <code>cor.test()</code>, and fitting a multiple regression with <code>lm()</code>.</div>
    </div>

  </div>

  <div class="pub-year-group">
    <div class="pub-year-header">Script 3</div>

    <div class="pub-item">
      <div class="pub-title"><a href="z_scores_ci.html">Z-Scores, Confidence Intervals, and the Z-Test</a></div>
      <div class="pub-venue">Standardizing scores with the z-score formula and <code>scale()</code>, finding areas under the normal curve with <code>pnorm()</code>, constructing 80/90/95/99% confidence intervals with <code>qnorm()</code>, and writing a custom <code>z.test()</code> function in R.</div>
    </div>

  </div>

  <div class="pub-year-group">
    <div class="pub-year-header">Script 4</div>

    <div class="pub-item">
      <div class="pub-title"><a href="t_tests.html">All About t-Tests</a></div>
      <div class="pub-venue">One-sample, independent samples (equal and Welch), and paired t-tests using a reading intervention dataset. Includes Levene's test for homogeneity of variance, bar graphs with error bars, and a demonstration of how the t-distribution converges to z as sample size increases.</div>
    </div>

  </div>

  <div class="pub-year-group">
    <div class="pub-year-header">Script 5</div>

    <div class="pub-item">
      <div class="pub-title"><a href="one_way_anova.html">One-Way Between-Subjects ANOVA</a></div>
      <div class="pub-venue">Testing whether reading time differs across device types (phone, tablet, laptop). Covers assumption checking (Shapiro-Wilk, Levene's test), fitting the model with <code>lm()</code> and <code>aov()</code>, eta squared as an overall effect size, and post-hoc comparisons with Tukey's HSD and Cohen's <em>d</em>.</div>
    </div>

  </div>

  <div class="pub-year-group">
    <div class="pub-year-header">Script 6</div>

    <div class="pub-item">
      <div class="pub-title"><a href="repeated_measures_anova.html">Repeated Measures (Within-Subjects) ANOVA</a></div>
      <div class="pub-venue">Testing whether blood pressure changes across four time points (Before, One Month, Three Months, Six Months) using the same participants. Covers the between-subjects vs. within-subjects distinction, reshaping data from wide to long format with <code>melt()</code>, assumption checking (normality of difference scores, sphericity), fitting the model with <code>aov()</code> and an <code>Error()</code> term, partial eta squared, Tukey's HSD via <code>emmeans</code>, confidence intervals, and Cohen's <em>d</em> for pairwise comparisons.</div>
    </div>

  </div>

  <div class="pub-year-group">
    <div class="pub-year-header">Script 7</div>

    <div class="pub-item">
      <div class="pub-title"><a href="two_way_anova.html">Two-Factor Between-Subjects ANOVA</a></div>
      <div class="pub-venue">Testing the effects of device type (Phone, Tablet, Laptop) and lighting condition (Blue, White, Yellow, Natural) on reading time in a 3 × 4 factorial design. Covers recoding factor levels with <code>factor()</code>, interaction plots, fitting the model with a <code>Device * Light</code> term, interpreting the ANOVA table (main effects and interaction), partial eta squared, and how a non-significant interaction guides the decision to interpret main effects directly. Post-hoc section uses Tukey's HSD via <code>emmeans</code> with confidence intervals and Cohen's <em>d</em> for pairwise comparisons of both factors.</div>
    </div>

  </div>
